matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, compute the numeric value of each side of the equation and confirm they are equal; without this, a visually plausible equation may still be mathematically false.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a candidate equation has been formed, before outputting it.
matchstick.example: Accepting 'XV - XVI = XV' which evaluates to -1 = 15.

matchstick.title: Preserve valid numeral shapes
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from or added to a Roman numeral, the resulting shape must correspond to a legitimate Roman‑numeral glyph; otherwise the character becomes invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During the stick‑move step, before finalizing the transformation.
matchstick.example: Removing the only vertical stick from an 'I' leaving no character, or forming a shape that does not match any Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator stick composition
matchstick.principle: Know the exact stick composition of each allowed operator (+ = vertical+horizontal, – = single horizontal, = = two horizontals); any change must result in one of these exact sets.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a stick from or to an operator.
matchstick.example: Removing the horizontal from '+' and leaving only a vertical line, which is not a permitted operator.

matchstick.title: Allowed operators only
matchstick.principle: The only operators permitted in the final equation are '+', '-', and '=', and you may not introduce any other symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any stick move, verify that every operator character matches one of the three allowed forms.
matchstick.example: Turning '+' into a 't' shape by adding an extra stick, which is not an allowed operator.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you cannot substitute a diagonal for a vertical or vice‑versa when moving it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When selecting a stick to relocate and when placing it on the destination character.
matchstick.example: Using a diagonal stick from an X to form the vertical part of an I.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; removing one leaves an invalid shape, so never use a diagonal from X or V as the source stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When choosing a source character for the stick move.
matchstick.example: Taking a diagonal from X, leaving a single diagonal line that is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect only the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains a stick); you must not alter any other characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During the planning of a move; ensure you are not implicitly changing more than two symbols.
matchstick.example: Changing 'XVIII' to 'XV' by removing three I’s, which touches more than two characters.

matchstick.title: Maintain a valid equality
matchstick.principle: The final equation must contain exactly one '=' sign, which must remain the standard two‑horizontal‑stick form; you may not delete, add, or alter it.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any stick move, check that the equality sign is still present and unchanged.
matchstick.example: Dropping the '=' sign entirely, leaving an expression like 'XV - XVI' with no equality.

matchstick.title: Operator stick transfers
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick involving an operator, consider transfers either between two operators or between an operator and a numeral, but ensure both the source and destination remain valid characters after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you cannot balance the equation by moving a stick only between numerals, explore moving a stick from an operator to another operator or to a numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' to turn it into '-', while also adding that stick to a numeral that becomes an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Validate Roman numeral syntax
matchstick.principle: Beyond shape, a Roman numeral string must follow standard ordering rules (e.g., no 'IXV'); after any transformation, parse each numeral to ensure it is syntactically valid before computing its value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after a stick move, before arithmetic checking.
matchstick.example: Creating the token 'IXV', which is shape‑wise possible but violates Roman numeral ordering.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes visual plausibility is enough and does not perform the arithmetic check.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always evaluate both sides numerically and confirm equality before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the stick count rather than the required shape for each numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that after removal or addition the character matches a known Roman numeral glyph.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets the exact stick composition of each operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Reference the operator stick composition rule before moving sticks involving operators.

matchstick.description: Moving sticks from X or V
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats all sticks as interchangeable.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never select a diagonal from X or V as the stick to move.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effectively removing a stick)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats the move as a deletion rather than a relocation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always specify both the source character (loses a stick) and the destination character (gains the same stick).

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model checks only character shapes, not the syntactic rules governing numeral sequences.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After a stick move, parse each numeral according to standard Roman numeral grammar and reject any that are not canonical.
